{
  "summary": "Hardens the read-only Berkeley DB parser used by wallet migration against crafted or corrupted databases. It tracks visited B-tree and overflow pages to reject multi-parent DAG traversal and infinite loops across empty overflow pages, and verifies that the sum of record lengths on a page does not exceed the page size. It also updates the BDB fuzz target to expect these new errors along with previously unhandled overflow errors.",
  "problem": "Malformed or malicious BDB files passed to `migratewallet` or `bitcoin-wallet` can trigger infinite loops, exponential traversal time, or huge memory inflation. Specifically, a page referenced by multiple parents causes redundant subtree traversal, empty overflow pages pointing to each other bypass length-based loop detection, and multiple index entries pointing to the same record duplicate memory allocation up to hundreds of megabytes.",
  "evidence": [
    "PR description: 'On master an ~8 KB file built this way doesn't finish.'",
    "PR description: 'A single 64 KB page can turn into ~500 MB this way. On master a 256 KB file took migratewallet from 54 MB to ~800 MB.'",
    "Commit 436ba919bd notes that page level checks stop direct ancestor cycles but small files can still describe exponential work through DAG structures."
  ],
  "dependencies": {
    "depends_on": [],
    "enables": []
  },
  "scope_notes": "Adds a byte-level mock BDB file generator (`BDBFileBuilder`) in `db_tests.cpp` to construct raw malformed and full B-tree pages for test cases without relying on Berkeley DB.",
  "changed_since_previous": "Added commit 2dfce13f9f updating `wallet_bdb_parser.cpp` to expect the new error strings as well as two previously missing overflow errors from #34959 that caused the fuzzer to abort.",
  "card": "This PR hardens the read-only BDB parser used by `migratewallet` and `bitcoin-wallet` against crafted files that bypass earlier checks. It prevents exponential traversal from multi-parent B-tree pages and infinite loops from cyclic empty overflow pages by tracking visited pages, and stops memory blowup by rejecting pages whose total record sizes exceed page bounds. The author demonstrates that an ~8 KB file can hang indefinitely on master and a 256 KB file can inflate memory usage to ~800 MB. The change includes unit tests with hand-crafted raw BDB binary layouts and updates the fuzz target to handle the new error strings.",

    "level": "medium",

    "why": "A mistake in BDB page traversal or record validation could cause valid legacy wallets to fail migration."

result.summary: Hardens the read-only Berkeley DB parser used by wallet migration against crafted or corrupted databases. It tracks visited B-tree and overflow pages to reject multi-parent DAG traversal and infinite loops across empty overflow pages, and verifies that the sum of record lengths on a page does not exceed the page size. It also updates the BDB fuzz target to expect these new errors along with previously unhandled overflow errors.
result.problem: Malformed or malicious BDB files passed to `migratewallet` or `bitcoin-wallet` can trigger infinite loops, exponential traversal time, or huge memory inflation. Specifically, a page referenced by multiple parents causes redundant subtree traversal, empty overflow pages pointing to each other bypass length-based loop detection, and multiple index entries pointing to the same record duplicate memory allocation up to hundreds of megabytes.
evidence: PR description: 'On master an ~8 KB file built this way doesn't finish.'
PR description: 'A single 64 KB page can turn into ~500 MB this way. On master a 256 KB file took migratewallet from 54 MB to ~800 MB.'
Commit 436ba919bd notes that page level checks stop direct ancestor cycles but small files can still describe exponential work through DAG structures.
result.scope_notes: Adds a byte-level mock BDB file generator (`BDBFileBuilder`) in `db_tests.cpp` to construct raw malformed and full B-tree pages for test cases without relying on Berkeley DB.
result.changed_since_previous: Added commit 2dfce13f9f updating `wallet_bdb_parser.cpp` to expect the new error strings as well as two previously missing overflow errors from #34959 that caused the fuzzer to abort.
result.card: This PR hardens the read-only BDB parser used by `migratewallet` and `bitcoin-wallet` against crafted files that bypass earlier checks. It prevents exponential traversal from multi-parent B-tree pages and infinite loops from cyclic empty overflow pages by tracking visited pages, and stops memory blowup by rejecting pages whose total record sizes exceed page bounds. The author demonstrates that an ~8 KB file can hang indefinitely on master and a 256 KB file can inflate memory usage to ~800 MB. The change includes unit tests with hand-crafted raw BDB binary layouts and updates the fuzz target to handle the new error strings.

risk.why: A mistake in BDB page traversal or record validation could cause valid legacy wallets to fail migration.
